chapter: Wingy Manone and Bix in Chicago (retyped)
title: Breaking with Wingy Manone: the El Dorado and Bill Kennedy
summary: Hodes says the boxer Bill Kennedy told him Wingy was only taking advantage of him. At the El Dorado Wingy's false arm was torn off in an argument with the boss and the whole band quit. Hodes then moved in with Kennedy.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: You say your time with -- when he was over -- around 1931.
And you had worked together, made the record. Was there a place called the Cellar that you worked at during that period?

Yes, My Cellar was a place and the Three Deuces was a place. And Wingy and I broke up after the El Dorado Club. We had gone out to the El Dorado Club, we were still talking, but I had met a New Orleans kid by the name of Bill Kennedy, who was a pug, a fighter. He'd been a great fighter. Fought for the championship and all that. Lost, but he'd been a great lightweight fighter.

And he loved this music. There was a fascination between us. We liked each other. And he didn't like what was happening to between Wingy and me. He kept telling me that Wingy was just taking me. I was paying for my musical education, is what he was saying. And of course, in the El Dorado Club after that, we were still together, but this thing was going on underneath.

And it was at the El Dorado that Wingy got into an argument with the boss. And the boss grabbed him and tore his false arm off and threw it across the floor. Arm and coat. And Wingy got up to the band and he says, let's go. We all quit to a man. It was Freeman and the whole band. Krupa -- I know Krupa and Freeman were in that band together. We played the floor show, we played everything. And it was a great experience, great band.
So it was about that time that I decided I would go live with Bill, because I didn't -- I was beginning to get fascinated with living with him. And that style, that I could
go to work. Art was working with me when we were not working.

Controlling, very much. And Bill kind of broke us up. And I went to live with Bill. So I started drifting away. But Win. opened that My Cellar, and he had on piano. Had nothing for me, and I came down there to visit. And I was just fortunate that the same night I came down, Bix came down. And I just sat there and listened.
